    3. Deep Dive: Modifying FREM Models

    Part3-deep-dive-updateFREMmodel.Rmd

    Introduction

    A FREM model and its data set are tightly coupled: the covariates live in the data as dummy observations, and the control stream indexes them by FREMTYPE. Editing both by hand to add or remove a covariate is slow and easy to get wrong.

    updateFREMmodel() makes those changes for you.

    This deep dive demonstrates five capabilities:

    • Removing covariates from an existing model.
    • Adding new covariates to a model.
    • Appending new individuals to an existing FREM dataset.
    • Updating a model’s initial parameter estimates directly from a converged .ext file.
    • Adding a structural $THETA or an IIV to a converged model.

    1. Pre-requisite Setup

    First, we load the package. To ensure system reproducibility, we map all base files from the package’s extdata directory and explicitly route all generated artifacts into a secure temporary directory (tempdir()).

    library(PMXFrem)
library(dplyr)
library(data.table)

# Isolate all generated outputs
td <- tempdir()

# Define paths to validated example files
frem_model_path <- system.file("extdata/SimNeb/run31.mod", package = "PMXFrem")
frem_ext_path <- system.file("extdata/SimNeb/run31.ext", package = "PMXFrem")
frem_data_path <- system.file("extdata/SimNeb/frem_dataset.dta", package = "PMXFrem")
ffem_data_path <- system.file("extdata/SimNeb/DAT-2-MI-PMX-2-onlyTYPE2-new.csv", package = "PMXFrem")

# Copy base model and ext files into the temporary directory for safe manipulation
file.copy(frem_model_path, td)
#> [1] TRUE
file.copy(frem_ext_path, td)
#> [1] TRUE
model_in_td <- file.path(td, "run31.mod")

    2. Use Case 1: Removing Covariates

    You may sometimes need to remove covariates from an existing model. Here, we remove WT, SEX, and AGE from run31.mod.

    The function needs the model’s structural configuration: numNonFREMThetas (the number of structural fixed effects) and numSkipOm (the number of standard variances, such as IIV or RUV, that precede the FREM $OMEGA BLOCK). Left as NULL (the default) they are derived from the FREM model and its .ext via fremModelInfo(); if the model’s ;;;FREM CODE markers / $OMEGA BLOCK(N) disagree with the .ext the derivation stops and asks for explicit values. We pass them here for clarity.

    result_remove <- updateFREMmodel(
  strFREMModel      = model_in_td,
  strFREMData       = frem_data_path,
  strFFEMData       = ffem_data_path,
  cstrRemoveCov     = c("SEX", "WT", "AGE"),
  strNewFREMData    = file.path(td, "frem_data_simplified.csv"),
  numNonFREMThetas  = 7,
  numSkipOm         = 2,
  bWriteData        = TRUE, # Generate the updated dataset
  bWriteMod         = TRUE, # Generate the updated control stream
  quiet             = TRUE,
  cstrKeepCols      = c("ID", "TIME", "AMT", "EVID", "RATE", "DV", "FOOD", "FREMTYPE")
)

new_model_path_remove <- file.path(td, "run31_new.mod")
print(paste("Simplified model successfully written to:", new_model_path_remove))
#> [1] "Simplified model successfully written to: /tmp/RtmpxChbiL/run31_new.mod"

    What the call did:

    • The data set rows for the removed covariates are dropped and the remaining FREMTYPE values re-indexed, so the $ERROR block has no gaps to handle.
    • The covariance matrix ($OMEGA) and typical values ($THETA) are systematically adjusted.

    3. Use Case 2: Adding Covariates

    Next, we take the simplified model generated above and add a covariate (AGE) back. We explicitly set bRecodeDichotomous = TRUE as a standard practice to ensure any 2-level categorical covariates are safely zero-indexed.

    # Start from the model and data set written above
model_to_add_to <- new_model_path_remove
data_to_add_to <- file.path(td, "frem_data_simplified.csv")

# The function requires the corresponding .ext file for the input model
file.copy(file.path(td, "run31.ext"), file.path(td, "run31_new.ext"))
#> [1] TRUE

result_add <- updateFREMmodel(
  strFREMModel       = model_to_add_to,
  strFREMData        = data_to_add_to,
  strFFEMData        = ffem_data_path,
  cstrContCovsToAdd  = "AGE",
  strNewFREMData     = file.path(td, "frem_data_with_age.csv"),
  numNonFREMThetas   = 7,
  numSkipOm          = 2,
  bWriteData         = TRUE,
  bWriteMod          = TRUE,
  bRecodeDichotomous = TRUE, # Safely zero-indexes 2-level categorical factors
  quiet              = TRUE,
  cstrKeepCols       = c("ID", "TIME", "AMT", "EVID", "RATE", "DV", "FOOD", "FREMTYPE")
)

print(paste("Expanded model successfully written to:", file.path(td, "run31_new_new.mod")))
#> [1] "Expanded model successfully written to: /tmp/RtmpxChbiL/run31_new_new.mod"

    What the call did:

    • The base clinical data (strFFEMData) is scanned to extract the new covariate’s mean and variance, which seed the new $THETA and $OMEGA parameters.
    • Dummy observation rows (EVID=2) are appended to the dataset for the new covariate under a newly assigned FREMTYPE.

    4. Use Case 3: Adding New Individuals

    New subjects can be added to a converged model without changing the covariate matrix. Here, we simulate 10 new individuals and fold them into the dataset.

    # 1. Load the unmodified FREM and FFEM data sets
frem_df <- fread(frem_data_path, data.table = FALSE) %>% select(-ODV)
ffem_df <- fread(ffem_data_path, data.table = FALSE)

# 2. Simulate 10 new individuals by shifting IDs
ffem_new_ids <- ffem_df[ffem_df$ID <= 10, ]
ffem_new_ids$ID <- ffem_new_ids$ID + max(frem_df$ID)

# 3. Append the individuals to the dataset
result_new_ids <- updateFREMmodel(
  strFREMModel      = model_in_td,
  strFREMData       = frem_df, # Pass dataset directly via memory
  strFFEMData       = ffem_new_ids, # Include the new IDs
  strNewFREMData    = file.path(td, "frem_data_appended.csv"),
  numNonFREMThetas  = 7,
  numSkipOm         = 2,
  bWriteData        = TRUE,
  bWriteMod         = FALSE, # The NONMEM model logic does not change
  quiet             = TRUE,
  cstrKeepCols      = c("ID", "TIME", "AMT", "DV", "EVID", "RATE", "FREMTYPE"),
  cstrSetToZero     = c("AMT", "EVID", "RATE")
)

print(paste("Original Max ID:", max(frem_df$ID), "| New Max ID:", max(result_new_ids$data$ID)))
#> [1] "Original Max ID: 964 | New Max ID: 974"

    What the call did:

    • The algorithm expands the dataset horizontally, mapping the structural and covariate dummy rows for the new IDs while keeping the control stream untouched (bWriteMod = FALSE).

    5. Use Case 4: Updating Initial Estimates

    Due to the size of typical FREM models, it is not feasible to update initial estimates manually. The PsN tool update_inits can be used for this, or you can use updateFREMmodel to do it by specifying a “NoData” update.

    result_inits <- updateFREMmodel(
  strFREMModel       = model_in_td,
  strUpdateType      = "NoData", # Skip dataset processing entirely
  basenames_th       = c("CL", "V", "MAT", "D1", "FRELFOOD", "MATFOOD"),
  basenames_om       = c("RUV", "D1", "CL", "V", "MAT"),
  numNonFREMThetas   = 7,
  numSkipOm          = 2,
  bWriteData         = FALSE,
  bWriteMod          = TRUE,
  bWriteFIX          = TRUE, # Explicitly carry over FIX flags
  quiet              = TRUE
)

print("Control stream initial estimates successfully updated from the .ext file.")
#> [1] "Control stream initial estimates successfully updated from the .ext file."

    What the call did:

    • updateFREMmodel() parses the -1000000000 iteration row from the provided .ext file.
    • The $THETA, $OMEGA and $SIGMA blocks are replaced, with the basenames written alongside them as comments.

    6. Use Case 5: Adding a Structural THETA or an IIV

    The updates above change the covariates or the data. A model sometimes needs a change to its structural part instead: one more $THETA, or one more IIV on a parameter that did not have one.

    By hand that means renumbering every THETA(), ETA(), MU_ and COV reference after the new one – including the references inside the ;;;FREM CODE block and the ETAn columns of $TABLE – and putting the new $OMEGA inside the skip region rather than after the FREM block, where it would join the covariate matrix. addFremStructuralTheta() and addFremIIV() do that.

    addFremStructuralTheta() inserts the new $THETA at numNonFREMThetas + 1, immediately before the FREM covariate means, and with addEta = TRUE adds a matching IIV:

    res_theta <- addFremStructuralTheta(
  strFREMModel = model_in_td,
  parameter    = "KA2",
  thetaInit    = 0.5,
  addEta       = TRUE,
  omegaInit    = 0.04,
  bWriteMod    = FALSE,
  quiet        = TRUE
)

c(thetaIndex = res_theta$thetaIndex, etaIndex = res_theta$etaIndex)
#> thetaIndex   etaIndex 
#>          8          3

    KA2 is not assigned anywhere in $PK, so it is defined rather than modified. The definition is delimited, so it is clear what the function added:

    i <- grep(";; Begin added THETA", res_theta$model)
j <- grep(";; End added THETA", res_theta$model)
cat(res_theta$model[i:j], sep = "\n")
     ;; Begin added THETA
     TVKA2 = THETA(8)
     MU_3 = LOG(TVKA2)
     KA2 = EXP(MU_3 + ETA(3))
     ;; End added THETA

    A parameter that $PK already assigns is modified in place instead. That is what addFremIIV() does on its own, for the case where the new random effect needs no new structural parameter:

    res_iiv <- addFremIIV(
  strFREMModel = model_in_td,
  parameter    = "FREL",
  omegaInit    = 0.04,
  bWriteMod    = FALSE,
  quiet        = TRUE
)

cat(grep("^\\s*FREL\\s*=", res_iiv$model, value = TRUE), sep = "\n")
FREL = (TVFREL*FRELCOVTIME) * EXP(ETA(3))

    Both take the new eta at numSkipOm + 1 and return the updated counts, so the value to pass to the next call comes back with the result.

    Two things to know before using either on a real model:

    • The .ext and .phi are not migrated. Only the control stream is rewritten, so the model has to be re-estimated. Pairing the rewritten model with the old .ext is easy to do by accident, and fremModelInfo() warns when it sees it.
    • They refuse rather than write a model that is quietly wrong. A parameter assigned inside an IF would take the eta on one branch only; a model using $ABBR REPLACE labels cannot be renumbered safely; a $THETA line whose values straddle the insertion point is ambiguous. Each of these stops with a message naming the record and the line.
